explanation: The dot product packs the angle between two vectors into one number: a . b = |a||b|cos(theta), so dividing by the two lengths recovers cos(theta) directly. Drag the components of a and b to change their directions, and watch the projection of a onto b (green) — it is the shadow a casts along b, and the dashed line from a's tip to that shadow is always perpendicular to b. When the vectors point the same way the dot product (and projection) are largest; at 90 degrees they vanish.
bullets: a . b = |a||b|cos(theta): the dot product is positive for acute, zero for right, negative for obtuse angles.
The projection of a onto b is a's shadow along b; the leftover piece is perpendicular to b.
Length of proj_b a = (a . b)/|b|; it shrinks to 0 exactly when the vectors are orthogonal.
